kpi.wauInfo: How many unique therapists recorded at least one session in the last 7 days. That is the definition of WAU, so this tile deliberately ignores the selected range — the sparkline below it does not. Key engagement metric.
kpi.sessionsThisWeekInfo: Total therapy sessions uploaded during the current calendar week — from Monday 00:00 Polish time. Each session is one audio recording sent by a therapist.
kpi.activationRateInfo: What share of therapists who signed up in the selected period have already recorded a first session. Mind short ranges: someone who signed up yesterday has not had time to activate, so a 7-day window understates this by construction. High activation (>30%) over a longer window means onboarding works.
kpi.satisfactionRateInfo: Share of positive ratings (thumbs up) given to AI reports in the selected period. Target is >85%. A low score means reports are not meeting clinical expectations.
kpi.avgCostPerSessionInfo: How much it costs us on average to process one session from the selected period — transcription (STT) plus report generation (LLM), computed with the same formula as the Σ line on the chart beside it. Shown in USD because providers bill in dollars.
kpi.avgCostPerSessionInfoPln: How much it costs us on average to process one session — the sum of transcription (STT) and report generation (LLM) costs. Converted to PLN using the current NBP exchange rate.
kpi.monthlySttCostInfo: How much we paid for Speech-to-Text in the period selected above. Production runs on ElevenLabs Scribe v2 ($0.22/h ≈ $0.0037/min of audio); older sessions are priced at whichever provider actually transcribed them (Deepgram nova-3 $0.0092/min, Google Chirp 3 dynamic batch $0.003/min).
kpi.monthlySttCostInfoPln: How much we paid for Speech-to-Text in the period selected above. Converted to PLN at the NBP average rate.
kpi.monthlyLlmCostInfo: How much we paid for generating clinical reports in the period selected above. Each report is priced at the rate of the model that actually produced it (rate table in pkg/llmcost). Cost depends on transcription length (input) and report length (output).
kpi.monthlyLlmCostInfoPln: How much we paid for generating clinical reports in the period selected above. Converted to PLN at the NBP average rate.
kpi.avgTokenUtilInfo: What share of allocated token limits organizations consume across billing periods overlapping the selected range. This is a ratio of sums (used ÷ limit), not an average of percentages, so a large organization weighs more than a small one. For organizations with an account-level counter we use its full allocation so the same tokens are never counted twice. 80%+ means limits are well matched.
kpi.avgLatencyInfo: How many minutes it takes on average to process a session from audio upload to the FIRST finished report. Covers transcription and AI analysis; report regenerations are not counted again. Target: <5 minutes.
kpi.failureRate7dInfo: What share of sessions in the selected period failed (e.g. transcription error, AI timeout, corrupted audio). The denominator is sessions in a terminal state — completed and failed; sessions still processing or cancelled by the user do not deflate the number. Target: <2%.
kpi.relabelRateInfo: How often therapists manually correct automatic speaker assignment (e.g. swapping 'Speaker 1' with 'Speaker 2') in the selected period. A high rate means diarization needs work.
kpi.retention30dInfo: What share of therapists are still recording sessions four weeks after signing up. Computed over a FIXED 26-week window, independent of the range above — with a short range no cohort would be mature yet. Weighted by cohort size; cohorts nobody returned to count as zero. >40% is a good B2B SaaS result.
kpi.avgSessionDurationInfo: The average duration of recorded therapy sessions uploaded to the system. Helps monitor if therapists are recording standard-length clinical sessions (e.g. 50 minutes) or only short summaries.
kpi.totalFixedCostsInfo: Total monthly fixed costs for GCP (Google Cloud Platform) and Firebase infrastructure.
kpi.gcpFixedCostsInfo: Total monthly fixed costs for GCP infrastructure (e.g. Cloud SQL instance, storage, KMS keyring).
kpi.firebaseFixedCostsInfo: Total monthly fixed costs for Firebase infrastructure (e.g. SMS authentication, hosting, Firestore baseline).
kpi.readMedianInfo: Half of therapists read a report for less than this. Time is ACTIVE — the counter pauses when the app goes to the background. A short median with a long p90 means most people skim while a minority read carefully.
kpi.readP90Info: The value 90% of reads stay below. Compared with the median it shows the spread: if p90 is a multiple of the median, there are two distinct groups of users.
kpi.readAbandonedInfo: Share of report opens with no matching finish — the user left the screen. A high value suggests the report fails to hold attention or loads too slowly.
kpi.sharedPctInfo: Share of completed sessions whose report the therapist sent to the client. This measures use of the product's differentiating feature.
kpi.inviteAcceptedInfo: Share of client-app invitations the client accepted. The rest expired or were revoked.
kpi.inviteMedianHoursInfo: Median time from sending an invitation to the client accepting it. A value near zero means clients accept immediately — usually during the session, with the therapist present.

chart.fixedCostsBreakdownDesc: Fixed cost allocation by provider (GCP vs Firebase)
chart.fixedCostsBreakdownInfo: Distribution of baseline fixed costs between Google Cloud Platform and Firebase.
chart.sessionsTrendInfo: This chart shows how many therapy sessions entered the system each week. A rising trend means growing product adoption. Drops may indicate holidays or technical issues.
chart.registrationsTrendInfo: How many new therapist accounts were created each week. Compare with marketing campaigns — spikes should correlate with landing page activity.
chart.planDistributionInfo: Pie chart showing how many organizations use each plan (Discovery, Growth, Mastery). Helps plan revenue and segment customers.
chart.costTrendDesc: STT + LLM cost per session, weekly (USD)
chart.costTrendInfo: Bars show transcription cost (STT, green) and report generation cost (LLM, orange) each week. The line is total cost. All amounts in USD.
chart.costTrendInfoPln: Bars show transcription cost (STT, green) and report generation cost (LLM, orange) each week. The line is total cost. Converted to PLN using the NBP exchange rate.
chart.tokenUsageDesc: Input and output tokens per week
chart.tokenUsageInfo: How many 'tokens' (text units) we send to the AI model (input = session transcript) and how many we get back (output = generated report). Large input with small output = long sessions, short reports.
chart.tokenUtilHeatmapDesc: Token usage as % of limit, per organization
chart.tokenUtilHeatmapInfo: The heatmap shows what share of its token limit each organization consumes across the weeks of the selected period. Red = close to the limit. An empty cell means no measurement, not zero usage. Helps identify customers who need a larger plan.
chart.satisfactionTrendInfo: What percentage of therapists rated the AI report positively (thumbs up) in a given week. A drop below 85% signals that prompts or the model need improvement.
chart.latencyTrendInfo: Two lines: P50 (typical session — half are faster) and P95 (slowest 5% of sessions). If P95 is rising, something is slowing down the pipeline for large files.
chart.issueCategoriesInfo: Horizontal bar chart showing what therapists most often reject in AI reports — e.g., wrong speaker assignment, inaccurate summary, missing key topics.
chart.failureRateTrendInfo: What share of sessions in a given week did not produce a report (e.g. transcription error, timeout, corrupted file). The denominator is sessions in a terminal state, same as the tile beside it. Target: <2%. A rising trend is worth investigating.
chart.funnelInfo: The funnel shows how many people who signed up in the selected period move through each stage: signup → add a client → record a session → read the report → rate the report. Every step is counted on the same population, so the funnel cannot widen. A large drop between steps shows where users are lost.
chart.activationTimeDesc: Hours from signup to audio upload
chart.activationTimeInfo: Histogram of how many therapists from the selected period recorded their first session within 1 h, a day, three days, or later after signing up. If most wait >72 h, onboarding needs work.
chart.cohortRetentionInfo: Retention heatmap: rows are cohorts (signup week as ISO year-week), columns are subsequent activity weeks. The value is the % of the cohort that recorded a session that week. Empty cells are weeks before the cohort signed up, or missing data. Warm colours = good retention.
chart.uploadFailuresInfo: How often an audio upload fails (e.g. dropped connection, file too large, unsupported format). The percentage is relative to upload attempts. A high rate means an infrastructure or in-app UX problem.
chart.hourlyHeatmapInfo: Heatmap of which weekdays and hours (Polish time) therapists most often upload sessions. Helps plan maintenance windows and server scaling.
chart.modalityDistributionInfo: This chart shows which psychotherapeutic modalities (e.g. CBT, psychodynamic, humanistic) are most frequently used in recorded sessions. Helps identify the most popular report customization profiles.
chart.sessionDurationTrendInfo: Weekly trend of average session duration in minutes. Allows monitoring engagement and checking session length stability over time.
chart.readingPlatformsInfo: Distribution of platforms therapists open reports on. Shows where polishing the report screen pays off — and whether the web version is used at all.
chart.clientSharingDesc: Sessions completed, shared and hidden by the client
chart.clientSharingInfo: Three weekly series over the selected period: all completed sessions, those whose report was sent to the client, and those whose report the client hid. Hiding is a reception signal — the report arrived, but the client put it away.
chart.inviteFunnelInfo: What happens to invitations therapists send to clients. A large expired share means the invitation does not arrive or the client does not know what to do with it.
chart.pairingAttemptsDesc: How many tries a client needs
chart.pairingAttemptsInfo: Distribution of pairing-code attempts. A tail on the right means UI friction; all zeros mean the code causes no trouble.

prompts.title: Report prompts
prompts.banner: You are editing the modality prompt used to generate reports. Changes apply from the NEXT generated report and affect every therapist of this modality. Each save creates a new version — you can restore a previous one at any time.
prompts.discardConfirm: You have unsaved changes. Discard them?
prompts.nothingSelected: Select a modality from the list.
prompts.contextTitle: Where does this prompt land? (call-2 context)
prompts.contextBody: Your prompt is the FIRST block of the report-generation prompt. The surrounding elements (language rules, conciseness rules, RAG context, transcript) are fixed and not editable from the panel — they guarantee parser consistency and pipeline safety.
prompts.historyMore: Older versions exist — showing the 20 most recent.
prompts.saveDialogBody: The change will affect all new {code} reports. Describe the reason (stored in version history and the audit log).
prompts.restoreDialogBody: Version {version}'s text will be saved as a NEW version of the {code} prompt (history stays intact). Suggested reason: „restore version {version}”.
prompts.chatKeyHint: The lens changes the chat's language and analytic ordering — the task and rules live in per-intent prompts in code, and invariants are appended by Render() regardless of this field. Empty text disables the lens for this modality. {max, number}-char cap: room for concrete instructions (closed lists, calibration rules), still far tighter than the report prompt because the lens rides on every question, not once per report.

aiChat.switchBody: Takes effect without a deploy — instances pick it up within 30 seconds. Every change needs a reason and is recorded in the audit log.
aiChat.guidance: Restricting costs less operationally than switching off: the therapist keeps quote search and statistics, and loses only the generative functions. Switch off entirely when the problem might also affect the extractive paths. Crisis information stays visible either way.
aiChat.tauNote: The confidence threshold is calibrated on the evaluation set. Never lower it to reduce false refusals — that moves the boundary toward answering questions that should be refused.
aiChat.confirmDisableBody: Every query will be refused as unavailable. Crisis information stays visible. Give a reason — it goes to the audit log.
aiChat.confirmEnableBody: The chat will start answering in the current mode. Give a reason — it goes to the audit log.
aiChat.confirmRestrictBody: Conceptualization, progress assessment and intervention suggestions become unavailable and are replaced with source material. The rest of the chat is unaffected.
aiChat.confirmUnrestrictBody: Generative functions come back. Do this only once the cause of the restriction is understood and covered by a test in the evaluation set.

ontologies.title: Modality ontologies
ontologies.intro: Versioned ontology content: draft → in review → approved. Approval does NOT put a version into production — that is a separate decision by a Superwizor admin.
ontologies.noVersions: This modality has no ontology version yet.
ontologies.readOnlyApproved: An approved version is immutable. To make changes, use the button that creates a new draft.
ontologies.readOnlyReview: This version is in review and frozen — otherwise the reviewer would judge different content than they approve.
ontologies.saveBeforeSubmit: Save your changes before submitting for review.
ontologies.fourEyesHint: A version is not approved by its author — review needs a second pair of eyes.
ontologies.activateAdminOnly: Putting a version into production requires the Superwizor admin role.
ontologies.activateWarning: From this moment reports for this modality are generated on this ontology version. The change takes effect within 30 seconds and can be reverted by pointing at another version.

flash.reject: Version rejected and returned to drafts.

branch.title: Create a new draft?
branch.body: Content will be copied from {modality} {version}. The original stays unchanged.

submit.title: Submit for review?
submit.body: {modality} {version} will be frozen until a decision is made.

approve.title: Approve this version?
approve.body: {modality} {version}. Approving does not put it into production.

activate.title: Put into production?
activate.body: Reports for {modality} will start being generated on version {version}.

experimental.description: Reports built on an ontology experts have not yet approved — generated alongside the production report, for comparison. Not clinical material and excluded from statistics.
experimental.limitHint: One experimental report is a dozen-plus Pro model calls, and the in-app toggle generates one for EVERY new session. Maximum 50.
experimental.confirmEnableBody: Therapists in this organization will see the toggle in report settings and can generate reports on an unapproved ontology. Every such report carries a warning banner and never reaches the client panel.
experimental.confirmDisableBody: The toggle disappears from settings and new requests are refused. Reports already generated remain — remove them through the normal report deletion path.
experimental.confirmLimitBody: New limit: {value} reports per therapist per day. Failed generations count too — they cost model calls.
experimental.auditHelp: Appends the pipeline's full decision log (rejected findings with reasonings, violations, context) to the end of experimental reports. Applies from the NEXT generation — existing reports are unchanged.
experimental.confirmAuditEnableBody: Enable report audit for this organization? Every SUBSEQUENT experimental report will end with the pipeline's full decision log.
experimental.confirmAuditDisableBody: Disable report audit? Existing reports stay unchanged; new ones will omit the audit section.

ontologyWizard.title: New construct
ontologyWizard.idInvalid: the identifier must start with a letter and contain only lowercase letters, digits and underscores
ontologyWizard.definitionPlaceholder: The definition the model will rely on when mapping.
ontologyWizard.q1: Does this phenomenon have a closed list of possibilities?
ontologyWizard.q1Help: Yes if you can enumerate every variant — like the six contact interruptions. No if the content is a description or a quote.
ontologyWizard.q2: Can one fragment carry several labels at once?
ontologyWizard.q2Help: Yes if a single utterance can carry two phenomena at the same time — like two cognitive distortions in one sentence.
ontologyWizard.q3: Is this one concept, or a structure made of parts?
ontologyWizard.q3Help: A structure if the meaning only emerges from several elements together — like a polarity, which needs two poles.

ontologyForm.noConstructs: This ontology has no constructs yet.
ontologyForm.unparseable: This content cannot be loaded into the form. Switch to the YAML view to see what is wrong.
ontologyForm.definitionHelp: This is what reaches the model's context during mapping — the sharper the boundary, the fewer the confusions.
ontologyForm.noCatalogue: This construct has no closed catalogue — the content is a description or a quote.
ontologyForm.clearCatalogue: Remove the catalogue (content becomes a description)
ontologyForm.glossPlaceholder: gloss (optional): which concept this is, in one line
ontologyForm.multiLabel: One fragment may carry several values at once
ontologyForm.multiLabelHelp: E.g. a single sentence carrying two cognitive distortions.
ontologyForm.evidenceHelp: How much material must be present before a claim can exist at all. Below the threshold the model returns an insufficient-data answer rather than an overreaching claim.
ontologyForm.boundariesHelp: The densest information in the whole ontology: a construct's boundary is what defines it in practice.
ontologyForm.isNotHelp: Select the constructs it must be told apart from.
ontologyForm.requires: What must hold for this to make sense?
ontologyForm.requiresHelp: Without the selected constructs this one renders with a weaker wording rather than being dropped.
ontologyForm.noOtherConstructs: The ontology has no other constructs yet.
ontologyForm.confusionsHelp: A living registry — it grows from what the model actually got wrong. Each entry says what people write and what should be there instead.
ontologyForm.compositeNotYet: This construct is a composite. The parts editor arrives in the next step — for now edit them in the YAML view.
ontologyForm.compositeHelp: A composite is made of parts. Each points to a session fragment, a client entry or another construct.

ontologySlots.minComplete: How many parts must be filled
ontologySlots.minCompleteHelp: Below this count the composite does not form at all. It cannot exceed the number of defined parts.

ontologyDiff.title: What changed
ontologyDiff.noPrevious: This is the first version of this modality — there is nothing to compare against.
ontologyDiff.unreadable: One of the versions cannot be loaded. Compare them in the YAML view.
ontologyDiff.identical: The ontology content is identical. Differences in file formatting are not ontology changes.
ontologyDiff.wielokrotnoscWylaczona: Several values at once no longer allowed
ontologyDiff.katalogUsuniety: Catalogue removed — the content became a description

ontologyComposition.help: Weights control the ORDER of report sections — never their visibility. An empty section disappears on its own. A composition change goes through review just like a content change.
ontologyComposition.layoutNotice: This ontology uses a custom section layout (mirroring the legacy report). Edit order and titles in the YAML view — weights do not apply.

brandStatement.body: Superwizor AI helps mental health professionals reclaim their mental space for attentive sessions, supporting process continuity and a deeper understanding of the client.

problem.overline: The cost unseen in the calendar
problem.title: Most of the session is lost not during — but after.
problem.body: A theme you wanted to return to. A sentence that seemed important. A direction you agreed upon. You keep all this in your head until the next meeting — and with a full schedule, the head cannot carry every detail. It's not a matter of discipline, but the number of sessions.
problem.quote: Prevents losing 30 to 40% of the information that I lose when preparing notes manually.

rodo.q: How does GDPR and client data security work?
rodo.a: All personal and medical data is fully protected. Data is hosted in EU data centers (GCP Frankfurt/Warsaw). Data transmission is encrypted via SSL, and audio files are automatically purged from the servers immediately after transcription. Confidential database columns are additionally encrypted using envelope encryption.

dpa.q: Do I need to sign a Data Processing Agreement (DPA)?
dpa.a: Yes. In accordance with GDPR (Article 28), every therapist using Superwizor AI must sign a Data Processing Agreement (DPA). We provide a ready-to-sign, fully compliant template that you can sign electronically in one click directly inside the application's admin panel.

consent.q: How do I get client consent for recording and AI analysis?
consent.a: Recording sessions requires the client's explicit, informed consent. In the legal resources section of the app, you will find ready-to-download and printable templates for client consent forms covering session recording and AI-assisted analysis, prepared by medical data protection lawyers.

training.q: Does the AI learn from my recordings or transcripts?
training.a: Absolutely not. We run Vertex AI models within Google Cloud, which guarantees that none of your inputs (audio, transcripts, generated notes) are used for training, fine-tuning, or improving Google's or any third-party's AI models.

modality.q: For which psychotherapeutic modalities is Superwizor AI designed?
modality.a: The application is built for leading psychotherapy approaches, offering dedicated templates tailored specifically to your work. We fully support: Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT), Psychodynamic, Humanistic-Experiential (including Gestalt), Systemic, Integrative, and Solution-Focused Brief Therapy (SFBT/TSR). The system automatically adjusts the report structure and clinical terms to the core assumptions of your chosen modality.

vat.q: Will I receive a VAT invoice for my subscription?
vat.a: Yes. After each purchase or automatic subscription renewal, our billing system automatically generates and sends a full VAT invoice (including NIP/tax ID and company name) to your email address, ready for business expense accounting in Poland/EU.

afterSession.q: What do I receive after a session?
afterSession.a: After the session, you receive a transcript split by speaker and reports with the essence of the meeting: key observations, client homework, and topics worth exploring deeper. Before the next meeting, you get a short note allowing you to return to full context in minutes.

modalityStyle.q: Are reports tailored to my modality and working style?
modalityStyle.a: Yes. Reports are generated in the language of your therapeutic modality. You can also adjust length, tone, and the number of session quotes. The report organizes session material, while therapeutic interpretation and decisions always remain yours.

sessionThreads.q: Does the app connect threads across sessions?
sessionThreads.a: Yes. Recurring topics from subsequent meetings are semantically linked with the client's previous context. This makes it easy to track how the process develops over time and return to the next session with full context.

supervisionScope.q: Does this replace supervision or my clinical work?
supervisionScope.a: No. Superwizor AI does not conduct therapy, make diagnoses, or replace supervision. It helps organize session material, recalls context, and supports preparation for the next meeting or supervision. Interpretation and therapeutic decisions always belong to you.

audioHandling.q: What happens to the session recording?
audioHandling.a: The recording is used solely to prepare the transcript. Immediately after creation, it is automatically and permanently deleted. Only the transcript and report remain in the app.

dataSecurity.q: How is client data security handled?
dataSecurity.a: Session data is encrypted and processed on infrastructure located within the European Union. We do not use it to train AI models or for any purpose other than providing the service. We operate in compliance with GDPR, treating therapeutic confidentiality as the foundation of our system.

clientConsent.q: How do I get client consent for recording?
clientConsent.a: Recording takes place strictly with informed client consent. It is helpful to calmly explain why the recording is made, what happens to it after transcription, and how it benefits the therapeutic process. We have prepared ready-made materials and consent templates to facilitate this conversation.

pricingTrial.q: How much does it cost and can I try it first?
pricingTrial.a: You start for free: the Exploration plan includes 30 days and 10 sessions, no credit card required. Paid plans start at 99 PLN per month (incl. VAT). All plans offer the same features — differing only in the number of included sessions.

cancellation.q: How do I start and can I cancel anytime?
cancellation.a: Create an account and you can start working in minutes. You can cancel your subscription at any time. You retain access until the end of your paid period, with no hidden terms or extra formalities.
